---
title: "Bioconductor Infrastructure"
---

This site documents the infrastructure behind bioconductor.org: what runs today, what is
replacing it, and the contracts between the pieces. It exists because none of it was
written down anywhere a newcomer — or a future maintainer — could find in one place.

## TL;DR

**Since 2026-09-28, bioconductor.org is served by the new stack.** The replacement estate is
a set of repos that meet at **data contracts rather than shared machines**, which is why each
can proceed — or be replaced — without stopping the others.

| Repo | What it is | Retires | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [bioc-registry](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry) | The data plane: an r-universe observer plus the propagation gate that decides *which build is fit to publish and what is true about a package*, exposed as an installable repository and a Parquet archive. It publishes at its own host; bioconductor.org does not serve from it yet ([registry switch](registry-switch.qmd)) | Planned: the three builders and the legacy build system. Today bioconductor.org's packages still come from BBS and r-universe through master ([how it works](how-it-works.qmd#publishing)) | [![freshness](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/actions/workflows/freshness.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/actions/workflows/freshness.yml) |
| [bioc-website](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-website) | The builder: a Python pipeline and an Astro static build that render package truth into ~93,000 pages, published immutably by CI | The master and staging webservers | [![site](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-website/actions/workflows/site.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-website/actions/workflows/site.yml) |
| [bioc-edge](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge) | The serving side: a Cloudflare Worker and the R2 mirror behind `bioconductor.org`, owner of the route table that decides *what is served where* | CloudFront, the S3 bucket, the Open Storage Network buckets | [![health](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/actions/workflows/health.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/actions/workflows/health.yml) |
| bioc-traffic (private) | Downstream of the request logs. Today: the daily check that yesterday's logs arrived, and log analysis. Planned: traffic classification (bioc-traffic#5), then download statistics from it. Published statistics still come from the legacy pipelines ([download stats](download-stats.qmd)) | The legacy download-stats pipelines | Not yet producing statistics |
| [bioc-build](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-build) and [bioc-manifest](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-manifest) | The standalone build system for the packages r-universe doesn't build, and the reviewed manifest that authorizes what it builds ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-two-new-repos-for-the-build-system-and-the-manifest-name.md)) | The legacy build machines, for data and workflow packages | Proof of concept |
| [bioc-infrastructure](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure) | This documentation site | Nothing. It is the map. | [![docs](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/actions/workflows/docs.yml) |

Two prototypes are archived (read-only) since 2026-09-29: [bioc-cloudflare](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-cloudflare), whose history continues in bioc-edge, and [bioc-origin](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-origin). Older pages and ADRs link to their issues, which remain readable; a mention of bioc-cloudflare as where code lives means bioc-edge today.

The **health** and **freshness** badges are daily probes of the live system, so red means
something is down or stale. The **site** and **docs** badges are build workflows; red means
the last build failed. More in [CI & scheduled jobs](ci.qmd). Where this is all going, milestone by
milestone: **the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd)**. How a request is answered and how content gets
published today, with the terms these pages use: **[how bioconductor.org works](how-it-works.qmd)**.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Live since 2026-09-28

`bioconductor.org` itself is served by the new stack, so there is nothing to configure:
`BiocManager::install()` works as it always has. If anything behaves differently from how it
used to, that's a bug we want to hear about. What has changed, with numbers:
**[What the new site has changed](improvements.qmd)**.
:::

### Where to file issues {#where-to-file-issues}

Report problems through the bioc-infrastructure issue forms. Reports get the `report`
label, are triaged by hand, and are moved to the repo that owns the problem.

- **A package won't install, can't be found, or a download fails** →
  [package install problem](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/new?template=install-problem.yml)
- **A page, download, redirect or file on bioconductor.org doesn't work** (for stale
  content, see [Edge cache](cache.qmd) first) →
  [something's broken on bioconductor.org](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/new?template=site-problem.yml)
- **Questions, doc corrections, or anything else** →
  [bioc-infrastructure issues](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues), or
  email [seandavi@gmail.com](mailto:seandavi@gmail.com). Suspected *security* issues go by
  email, never a public issue; see
  [bioc-edge's SECURITY.md](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## How the pieces meet

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  bbs["BBS<br/>source tarballs"] --> master["master.bioconductor.org"]
  ru["r-universe<br/>builds packages"] -- "most binaries" --> master
  master -- "bioc-sync, hourly" --> mir[("R2: the mirror")]
  site["bioc-website<br/>static build, CI"] --> b[("R2: site/&lt;sha&gt;")]
  mir --> wk["bioc-edge Worker<br/>build first, else mirror"]
  b --> wk
  wk --> v(["bioconductor.org"])
  ru -- "polled every 15 min" --> reg["bioc-registry<br/>the propagation gate"]
  reg -. "own workers.dev host" .-> cran["installable R repository"]
  reg -. "DuckDB" .-> pq["Parquet archive"]
  reg -- "build-time fetch, /next/ pages only" --> site
  reg -. "planned: registry switch" .-> mir
```

Solid lines to `bioconductor.org` are the path that serves it today: packages come from
master through the hourly sync, and the registry is not in that path. Dashed lines are the
registry's own outputs and the [planned switch](registry-switch.qmd). Detail:
[how bioconductor.org works](how-it-works.qmd).

The organising principle is one idea applied at two scales: **define where the data comes
from once, and let every consumer render it.** Inside `bioc-website` that shows up as the
`astro/data/` seam between its pipeline and its renderer. Across the estate it shows up as
the table above. The website is one consumer of package truth. It is deliberately not the
place where "what is true about a package" gets decided.

## The contracts

Everything above holds together at five seams. They are worth stating in one place, because
each is a place where a change in one repo can quietly break another.

**1. `astro/data/` — pipeline to renderer**, inside `bioc-website`. JSON written to
disk by a Python pipeline, read by an Astro build. Nothing downstream knows where the data
came from; nothing upstream knows how it is rendered. That seam is what let the same
component render both the legacy-parity pages and the new data-plane-fed pages unchanged.

**2. The registry's HTTP API — data plane to website**, fetched at build time from
`/data/prop/{universe}/index.json`, `/data/state/{universe}/latest`, and
`/prop/{universe}/cas/{sha256}`. This is what the `/next/` pages render: what *propagated*,
not whatever r-universe last built.

**3. The R2 object layout — build to serving.** The website's CI writes immutable
`site/<sha>/` builds, a `site/latest` pointer, and `preview/pr-<n>/` for every pull request
(served at `/_pr/<n>/`).
The Worker reads them. **The build side publishes; the serving side decides what is served** —
write access to the website repo never implies the power to change production.

**4. The route table — `_routes.json`, an object in R2, not code.** Flipping a route from
mirrored legacy content to a static build is a data write; rolling it back is the same write
in reverse. No deploy, no rebuild. An empty table means the mirror serves everything, which
is the safe default. Since the cutover the table routes `/` to the latest build: the build
serves any path it has a file for, and the mirror copy in R2 serves the rest.

**5. Request logs — serving to statistics.** The Worker emits one structured record per
request in the same field vocabulary as the CloudFront logs it replaces, delivered by
Logpush to Google Cloud Storage, so both eras can be one query rather than a migration
project. Analysis lives in bioc-traffic (a private repo). The record keeps the raw client address; de-identification is a view, and
nothing published carries the address
([ADR 0012](adr/0012-client-addresses-are-stored-raw-and-hashed-in-views.md)).

## Where this stands

The serving replacement took over `bioconductor.org` on 2026-09-28: nameservers moved to
Cloudflare in the afternoon and the site followed that evening
([DNS runbook](dns-cutover.qmd)). The legacy servers still run behind it, and still produce
the content it mirrors, until [milestone M2](roadmap.qmd) retires them. Package landing pages
exist for 35 releases: 3.23 and 3.24 are regenerated, and the 33 older releases are a frozen
snapshot ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-old-releases-and-their-checkresults-are-archival.md),
[site build](astro-site-build.qmd)). The build-system track is earlier. Software source
tarballs are still built by BBS and most binaries by r-universe; serving them from the
registry instead is the [registry switch](registry-switch.qmd). Annotation, experiment-data
and workflow packages have no replacement builder running yet
([bioc-build](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-build) is a proof of concept).

Numbers throughout this site are point-in-time measurements, not live dashboards — **check
the date on each page** before relying on specifics.

### Two costs, not one

Two figures appear across these pages and they are not competing estimates of the same thing:

- **~$5,000/month** is the AWS estate being *retired* — CloudFront, the S3 bucket, and the
  master and staging webservers — before counting the builder hardware or the staff time to
  keep three operating systems patched.
- **$240-500/month** is the estimate for the Cloudflare stack replacing it, from production
  traffic on 2026-09-28. Storage is about $77 of that (5.1 TB in R2); the rest is per-request
  charges. R2 charges no egress fees, and egress is most of the difference
  ([details](improvements.qmd#costs-about-5000-a-month-down-to-a-couple-of-hundred)).

### Known weak points

Stated here rather than discovered later:

- **The website reads the registry's stored JSON shape directly**, not a versioned API. An
  unreachable endpoint fails the build loudly, which is right; a *renamed field* renders a
  blank section on a page and fails nothing. The convention is "never change a shape in
  place, add fields and tolerate absences" — it is a convention, with no mechanism behind it.
- **`astro/data/` has no written schema.** Its shape is implied by the code that writes it
  and the code that reads it, and by nothing else.
- **The 15-minute poll has no fast alerting.** A silent stop is caught by bioc-registry's
  daily freshness check, which fails when the latest observation is more than 36 hours old
  (the freshness badge above).
- **Some facts are written in several places** — release numbers, repository lists, display
  labels — and at least one set of display labels already disagrees with itself.

## How this site is organised

The pages fall into two kinds, and the sidebar separates them:

- **The new system** — pages that describe the replacement estate and should still be true,
  with only numbers to refresh, once the transition completes:
  [how bioconductor.org works](how-it-works.qmd), [what it has changed](improvements.qmd), [installing packages](install.qmd),
  [running a mirror](mirror-how-to.qmd), the [DNS runbook](dns-cutover.qmd), the
  [edge cache](cache.qmd), the
  [site build](astro-site-build.qmd), the [propagation gate](propagation-gate.qmd), and the
  r-universe half of the build estate: its [size limits](r-universe-size-limits.qmd) and the
  [data-package size audit](data-packages-in-r-universe.qmd) behind the standalone build
  system ([bioc-build](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-build)).
- **The legacy system (historical)** — dated snapshots of the BBS-era estate and the record
  of the transition away from it: [what ran on staging and master](current-state.qmd),
  [legacy propagation and the push hooks](legacy-propagation.qmd), the
  [builder transition](builder-transition.qmd), the measurement pages on
  [VIEWS](views-and-r-universe.qmd), [package pages](reproducing-package-pages.qmd) and
  [download stats](download-stats.qmd), the [R2 migration](r2-migration.qmd) and the
  [decommission plan](decommission-plan.qmd). These are kept as history — corrected if
  wrong, but not updated to track the system. Pages about the new system may cite them;
  nothing new should depend on them.

If you want the reasoning rather than the description, the
[ADRs](adr/0008-three-repos-and-a-strangler-migration.md) are the honest record —
including the decisions that were later reversed.

::: {.callout-note}
This site is deliberately public, so that the people affected by this work can read it
without needing an account or an invitation. Findings are shared with the Bioconductor core
team as they land, so read these pages as work in progress rather than settled conclusions.
:::
